agingcare_banned.finding: AgingCare.com is owned by A Place For Mom (APFM) — Assistedly.ai's primary competitor
agingcare_banned.tos_violation: Their Terms of Use explicitly prohibit 'Using the Sites for commercial purposes'
agingcare_banned.recommendation: REMOVE AgingCare.com entirely from playbook. Replace with AARP Community, Family Caregiver Alliance, Mass.gov resources, or local Facebook Groups.

human_in_the_loop_required.finding: All five platforms explicitly prohibit automated posting, scraping, and bot behavior
tos_citations: Reddit: 'Scraping without prior written consent is prohibited'
Quora: 'Accessing data through automated means for commercial purposes' prohibited
Facebook: 'Posting automatically at high frequencies' prohibited
Nextdoor: 'Use of scripts, robots, crawlers to scrape' prohibited
AgingCare: 'Screen scraping, database scraping, web bots' prohibited
human_in_the_loop_required.recommendation: AI can draft; HUMAN must manually post every comment. No automated DMs. No scraping for ongoing operations.

real_identity_required.finding: Fictional personas violate platform rules on Facebook, Reddit, and Nextdoor
tos_citations: Facebook: 'Provide the same name you use in everyday life'
Reddit: Impersonation/misrepresentation rules prohibit fictional personas
Nextdoor: Address verification required; must be real resident
real_identity_required.recommendation: Hire or designate a REAL person as Pat. If using brand voice, create business pages (Facebook Page, Nextdoor Business Page).

single_account_rule.finding: Multiple accounts for same entity = 'coordinated inauthentic behavior' (Facebook) or ban evasion (Reddit)
single_account_rule.recommendation: Consolidate Pat and Maggie into ONE disclosed identity per platform. Maggie is an AI assistant disclosed in bio, not a separate account.

winning_bot_pattern.finding: AI bots excelling on these platforms ALL use human-in-the-loop model
examples: Claude Routines: AI monitors → drafts → human reviews → manual posts
ReplyAgent.ai: AI finds threads → drafts → human edits → manual post
Long Game AI: AI tracks conversations → human builds relationship → manual outreach
winning_bot_pattern.key_principle: AI-Augmented Human, Never AI-Only. Platforms ban fully automated behavior but tolerate AI-assisted human posting.

compliant_operating_model.description: Revised playbook structure that complies with all platform ToS
steps: 1. Real person uses ONE account per platform (real name on Facebook/Reddit, business page on Nextdoor)
2. AI monitors platforms using native search (no scraping) and drafts responses
3. Human reviews every draft, personalizes 80%+, adds specific context from the post
4. Human manually posts every comment from their own account
5. Human responds to all replies and builds rapport
6. Only when user explicitly asks for more help, human sends a single DM
7. In DM, human discloses Maggie (AI assistant) and asks for opt-in to SMS
8. Maggie (AI) handles SMS fulfillment after explicit opt-in, always disclosing AI status
9. Pat never mentions AI or brand names in public comments; Maggie always discloses in first text
